abstract: Audits airside ramp equipment readiness, high-loader fleet capacity, and aircraft-to-warehouse transit speed
system_message:
You are Ramp operations superintendent (RAMP). The Ramp operations superintendent (RAMP) audits airside ramp equipment readiness, high-loader fleet capacity, and aircraft-to-warehouse transit speed, as well as aircraft de-icing support operations across prospective cargo handlers.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Aircraft de-icing support（DEICE）
information_points.content:
RAMP-DEICE-8U3：According to winter operations fleet logs, Aerocold Atlantic Alliance recorded a de-icing truck response latency of 8 min from the ramp dispatch call to vehicle arrival at the aircraft stand.
RAMP-DEICE-O4R：During winter schedule trials, Trans-Celtic CoolPort Consortium registered a de-icing truck response latency of 16 min from dispatch to on-stand arrival.
RAMP-DEICE-3LP：Hibernia BioLogistics Group logged a de-icing truck response latency of 12 min between ramp dispatch and arrival at the aircraft stand during winter schedule trials.

information_points.title: Audits airside ramp equipment readiness, high-loader fleet capacity, and aircraft-to-warehouse transit speed（APRON）
information_points.content:
RAMP-APRON-E8K：For Hibernia BioLogistics Group evaluated over the trailing 30-day window, the dual-temperature high-loader fleet count is 4 units stationed at the North Cargo Apron, and the baseline tarmac transfer run duration is 26 min along the designated airside service road route.
RAMP-APRON-J0I：For Aerocold Atlantic Alliance over the trailing 30-day window, the dual-temperature high-loader fleet count stands at 8 units of fully operational equipment stationed at the North Cargo Apron, and the baseline tarmac transfer run duration is 18 min for loaded refrigerated dollies en route from the furthest long-haul cargo stand to the reception bay.
RAMP-APRON-IA6：For Trans-Celtic CoolPort Consortium over the trailing 30-day window, the ground support equipment register records a dual-temperature high-loader fleet count of 8 units, and GPS tracking logs a baseline tarmac transfer run duration of 26 min from the furthest long-haul cargo stand to the North Cargo Apron reception bay.
RAMP-APRON-00X：Auditing Aerocold Atlantic Alliance across the trailing 12-month window indicates a dual-temperature high-loader fleet count of 10 units stationed at the North Cargo Apron, alongside a baseline tarmac transfer run duration of 14 min.
